C9000050.statement: Adversarially audit, verify, or refute OpenAI Manuscript Family 050 (A counterexample to Griffiths’ positivity conjecture.; papers: Ample rank-two bundles on the quadric surface without Griffiths-positive metrics; Lean status: Partially/Comparator formalized (lean/docs/050.md)): either (a) discover and certify an explicit mathematical flaw, sign/orientation error, counterexample to an intermediate lemma, or statement-fidelity/citation gap with a deterministic symbolic/computational certificate (`verify.py` + `exact_certificate.json`), or (b) independently verify, repair, or generalize the manuscript's core mathematical theorem with a standalone machine-checkable certificate certified by the independent Reviewer.

C_MAIN_050.statement: The graph bundle has E_m ample for every m but no strictly Griffiths-positive metric for all sufficiently large m.

C_CONSTRUCTION_050.statement: The graph identifications descend at the nodes and define a locally free rank-two equalizer bundle with both line quotients and dual gluing.

C_AMPLENESS_050.statement: For every m>=1, E_m is ample; O_{P(E_m)}(n) is very ample for every even n with n-1>=3m.

C_LIMIT_050.statement: For arbitrary positive-rank G on S, infinitely many positive twisted pullbacks imply a nonzero finite psh Hermitian quadratic on every fiber of G dual.

C_TRACE_050.statement: On (P^1)^d, d>=1, with integer twist a, the m^{-d} ramified trace is continuous and jointly psh, positive Hermitian quadratic on every fiber, and transforms by |g|^{2a/m}.

C_STRONG_050.statement: On any compact complex base, normalized vanishing-twist psh quadratics admit strong coefficient convergence in every finite L^p_loc with untwisted limit transitions.

C_REP_050.statement: Monotone base convolution and finite polarization recover a unique finite psh Hermitian quadratic on every fiber, invariant under changes of chart.

C_MAX_050.statement: The canonical limit satisfies 0<=q(x,v)<=|v|_0^2 and attains value one on the background unit sphere, excluding total collapse.

C_GENERAL_050.statement: The limit theorem extends to (P^1)^d, arbitrary positive rank, semipositive input metrics, and integer twists a_j=o(m_j), with strong finite-L^p coefficient convergence and preserved normalized maximum.

C_OBSTRUCTION_050.statement: For the graph-defined bundle every finite nonnegative psh function quadratic on every dual fiber is zero, via ruling reduction, logarithmic curvature mass, and incompatible invariant measures.

C_MATRIX_DATA_050.statement: The specified lifts have traces and orders 6,6,8 as stated, no common eigenline, and an expanding product AB.

C_GRAPH_DIVISOR_050.statement: The three graphs form a reduced (3,3) divisor with exactly six transverse nodes and no triple intersection.

C_NODE_DESCENT_050.statement: Exponent 24 makes the fiber maps agree at nodes; nodal descent gives alpha and the local equalizer basis gives both line quotients.

C_SYM_FILTRATION_050.statement: Alternating quotient sequences give the stated locally free symmetric-power line filtration, including coincident kernel fibers and nonreduced pullbacks.

C_GENERATION_050.statement: For n even and n-1>=3m all graded bidegrees are nonnegative; H^1 vanishing lifts generators through the filtration.

C_EMBEDDING_050.statement: Evaluation, relative Veronese, the P base embedding and Segre have hyperplane pullback O_{P(E_m)}(n) with the stated quotient convention.

C_RULING_050.statement: Ruling reduction and the graph identities turn any nonzero everywhere-quadratic psh function into one nonzero A,B-invariant squared seminorm on O(-24).

C_LOGCURV_050.statement: Logarithmic weights are locally integrable and subharmonic, including zeros; their positive invariant measure on O(-b) has total mass 2*pi*b.

C_NO_INVARIANT_050.statement: Expansion by AB and order-three A,B with no common eigenline exclude a nonzero finite positive common invariant measure on P^1.

C_ALG_050.statement: The two-index polarization, generic two-dimensional congruence, normal-frame mixed jets and positive-modulus frame cancellation in verify.py are exact identities; finite fixtures are not analytic proofs.
